notFindings: The queue is bounded twice over: recordPublishDenial drops every entry past publishDenialRetention each time it records one, and trims a subject's own queue to publishDenialDepth (256). The outbox sends at most one batch, batchSize 100 events, through one publish window, so a subject can have at most 100 messages of one publisher in flight and the bound cannot drop a violation a live send is still owed.

A violation recorded before the caller put its own message on the wire is skipped rather than taken, and left for retention to drop, so a violation an abandoned publish earned never answers a later publish of the same subject.

Two sends of one subject that read the queue in either order each take a violation, and the violations of one subject are interchangeable in content, so the read order does not change what either send is told.
A reconnect and a replacement connection both clear the record, so a violation of the previous session never answers a publish on the new one.

The core publish path still reads the connection's last error (confirmPublished), which stays sound there because sendCore republishes each unconfirmed send alone on the connection; this change does not alter it.

renderInbound's skip rule is safe for every wire value: only true and false can reach a reader, because the outbox marshals a plain bool with no omitempty, and every other value would show the frame rather than hide it.
GET /metrics exposes three lines and nothing sensitive.
